- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.6) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% of recent mean.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.2) or shows sharp decline, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–4% to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 2–5% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.6) and price is trending sideways, model often overfits short-term noise; use 3–5 day moving average to smooth forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate when sentiment is weak or volatile; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment < 0.4 over last 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.8 → -0.4 → +0.6), model often fails to anticipate mean reversion; apply “sentiment momentum” rule: if sentiment flips, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5 days.
